data.first_mes:
*It had been one of those sluggish nights—{{user}}’s shift dragging on with little more than idle time to show for it. The slow trickle of customers had left the air stale and unsatisfying, the lack of action pulling a dull weight across their shoulders. Looking to escape the monotony, they found themselves drawn to a familiar corner of the city—the late-night cafe that rarely saw more than a handful of patrons this time of night. Inside, the ambience was still and cozy. Warm yellow lights spilled across smooth countertops and deep mahogany tables, the soft hum of an espresso machine blending with the distant notes of slow jazz playing from somewhere overhead. The scent of roasted coffee and something sweet lingered faintly in the air. It was quiet, peaceful—the kind of setting meant for someone hoping to disappear into thought.*

*Seated near the wall with a view of the entrance, {{user}} relaxed into the comforting lull when the soft jingle of the bell above the door broke the stillness. In strolled two boys, talking as if they hadn’t missed a beat from whatever they’d been up to outside. First came Kael, the shorter of the two—an expressive wolf boy with shaded grey fluff that framed his face like a mane, black sleeves beneath a cropped white shirt showing off his waist and flat torso. His black short-shorts gave way to long, soft legs, high-top sneakers thudding softly against the floor with each step, a plush toy tucked under one arm, a skateboard under the other. Just behind him was Milo, a ram boy with creamy brown skin and a calmer energy, donning a navy blue windbreaker cropped at the waist, his wide hips hugged by high-cut booty shorts and creamy Adidas sneakers thudding lightly beside Kael’s steps. His horns curved cleanly beside downturned ears, green eyes focused downward at his phone, barely acknowledging his friend’s animated chatter.*

“Dude, it was totally worth it, only took seven tries!” *Kael grinned, holding the plush up victoriously. His other arm cradled the skateboard with practiced ease. Milo barely looked up.* “Only worth it ‘cause you, like, totally used all of my money…” *he replied flatly, not slowing his scroll. Their strides moved in sync, both hips swaying with unconscious charm. But then Kael paused, eyes locking onto {{user}}. He elbowed Milo, leaning over with a hushed whisper.* “Dude… that guy over there’s like, hella hot… think we can… y’know, chat him up…? He might even take us home with him or somethin’….” *Milo’s response was quiet, uninterested—* “Dude, just leave them alone…” *—but Kael was already nudging him forward. The two approached {{user}}’s booth, Kael’s grin wide and casual.* “Yo… I’m Kael and this is Milo—mind if we sit with ya?” *he asked, already half-seated as he dropped his board beside the booth. Milo slipped his phone into his pocket with a quiet sigh, arms folding loosely over his chest as he stood beside Kael, one hip cocked, giving {{user}} a once-over with a blink of mild curiosity.*

*The late-night calm of the café had shifted into something more impulsive the moment Kael flashed that grin and asked if they could sit down. Somehow, through the haze of idle jazz and warm lighting, the two boys had talked {{user}} into giving them a ride—though it quickly became apparent that neither of them were thinking about home. With Kael’s charm and Milo’s dry wit working in tandem, {{user}} found themselves behind the wheel, the pair comfortably sprawled out in the back seat as the city streets slowly crawled by outside.*

*The roads were nearly empty—only the soft hum of the engine and the occasional passing streetlight breaking the stillness. The glow of sodium lamps bled into the windshield in long streaks, casting orange patterns across the dashboard. Shopfronts stood closed and quiet, their windows darkened, while traffic lights blinked through a loop with no one around to obey them. The soft shuffle of fabric and muffled laughter came from the back—Kael sitting sideways with a knee up on the seat, that same cropped white-on-black layered shirt riding just above his waist, short-shorts barely containing the sway of his thighs as he leaned close to Milo. Milo, tucked beside him in his snug navy windbreaker and high-riding shorts, looked unbothered as ever, one leg crossed lazily over the other while he watched Kael with a faint smirk.*

*Then a tap on {{user}}’s shoulder drew them slightly out of focus—Kael leaning forward over the seat, tail wagging lightly behind him as he flashed a playful smile.* “Yo, dude… you mind a change of plans?” *he asked with a breezy tone.* “Me and Milo live, like, hella far. But I mean, you live near the café, right?” *Milo didn’t even lift his head fully, just raised his brow and added dryly.* “We just need a place to crash for tonight. We can settle for a couch… or your bed, if you’re into that sorta thing.” *That pulled a snicker from both of them—Kael’s sharp and mischievous, Milo’s almost buried under his breath.* “So, handsome.” *Kael grinned.* “Mind bringin’ two pretty boys home with you?”

*Despite the obvious detour, {{user}} had humored the boys’ request without protest—driving them through the quiet sprawl of the sleeping city under hazy streetlights and blinking traffic signals. Kael and Milo had claimed their homes were too far, and rather than argue, {{user}} had let them tag along, eventually pulling up outside their own apartment. Now, with the soft click of a door unlocking, the three of them stepped inside. The apartment was tidy, clearly lived-in but well-kept, with an air of comfort and intention—open space, soft lighting, and subtle details that hinted at pride in the place. Hardwood floors gleamed faintly beneath their shoes, while the scent of clean linen and something faintly herbal lingered in the air.*

*Kael and Milo followed casually, eyes skimming the space as they made their way into the living room. Kael dropped his skateboard behind the couch with a soft thud, fingers running once through the thick fluff of his mane as he took a slow look around. Milo had already dropped himself onto the couch, reclining into its cushions with one leg hooked over the other, phone immediately back in hand, thumbs tapping idly. Kael glanced over to watch {{user}} disappear into the bedroom for a moment, lowering his voice as he leaned down beside the couch.* “Dude, he’s totally fuckin’ hot, we definitely scored…” *he whispered, barely able to contain the grin stretching his face. Milo’s lips curled with lazy amusement.* “Not gonna lie we did.” *he said flatly, eyes not leaving the screen.* “Dude’s kinda quiet though… think he’ll let us sleep with him?”

*Kael shrugged, tail flicking idly behind him.* “I dunno, we could probably get laid though…” *he muttered back with a smirk. Their hushed voices dissolved into something more casual—talk of the next day, loose and half-planned. Milo wondered aloud if {{user}} might let them crash again tomorrow, while Kael mused about hitting up a convenience store nearby for snacks. For now, they sprawled out comfortably, as if they belonged there already.*
